'''Robert Christopher Franks Jr.''' (born December 18, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Ibaraki Robots]] of the [[B.League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State Cougars]].

==Early life==
Franks grew up in [[Vancouver, Washington]] and attended [[Evergreen High School (Vancouver, Washington)|Evergreen High School]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Valencia |first=Paul |date=2023-06-19 |title=Pro basketball player Robert Franks Jr. always has time for Vancouver and Evergreen High School - ClarkCountyToday.com |url=https://www.clarkcountytoday.com/people/pro-basketball-player-robert-franks-jr-always-has-time-for-vancouver-and-evergreen-high-school/ |access-date=2025-06-09 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-08-08 |title='Roller coaster' pro career has taken Washington State's Robert Franks from G-League title to NBA to Australia's NBL |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2022/aug/08/roller-coaster-pro-career-has-taken-washington-sta/ |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=Spokesman.com |language=en}}</ref> where he was a captain of the school's basketball team for his final three years. As a junior, he averaged 19 points and eight rebounds per game and was named All-Region by ''[[The Columbian]]'' and honorable mention Class 4A  All-State by the [[Associated Press]]. Rated a three star recruit and one of the 25 top recruits in the state by ''[[The Seattle Times]]'', Franks committed to play college basketball at Washington State University going into his senior year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blogs.seattletimes.com/take2/2014/01/03/high-school-basketball-washingtons-top-25-boys-recruits/|title=High school basketball: Washington's top 25 boys recruits|first=Kevin|last=Cacabelos|website=[[The Seattle Times|SeattleTimes.com]]|date=January 3, 2014|access-date=July 24, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/highschoolsports/article/evergreen-of-vancouver-forward-robert-franks-verbally-commits-to-washington-state/|title=Evergreen of Vancouver forward Robert Franks verbally commits to Washington State|first=Nick|last=Daschel|website=[[OregonLive.com]]|date=September 24, 2014|access-date=July 24, 2019}}</ref> Franks was again named All-Region and honorable mention All-State as a senior.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dailyevergreen.com/46216/sports/athlete-of-the-week-robert-franks/|title=Athlete of the Week: Robert Franks|first=Shawn|last=O'Connor|work=[[The Daily Evergreen]]|date=January 22, 2019|access-date=July 24, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
Franks played four seasons for the [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State Cougars]], playing exclusively off the bench during his first two years with the team. He appeared in 23 games as a freshman, averaging 2.2 points per game and 8.3 minutes played. In his sophomore season, he appeared in all 30 of the Cougars games and averaged 6.3 points and 3.3 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.columbian.com/news/2018/mar/26/evergreen-grad-robert-franks-declares-for-nba-draft/|title=Evergreen grad Robert Franks declares for NBA draft|first=Micah|last=Rice|work=[[The Columbian]]|date=March 26, 2018|access-date=July 24, 2019}}</ref> He entered the starting lineup at the beginning of his junior year after losing over 25 pounds during the offseason.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2017/dec/15/return-of-the-deadeye-slimmed-down-robert-franks-s/|title=Return of the Deadeye: Slimmed-down Robert Franks shapes up as key Washington State player|first=Theo|last=Lawson|work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|date=December 15, 2017|access-date=July 24, 2019}}</ref> Franks finished the season 7th in the [[Pac-12 Conference]] with 17.4 points per game while also averaging 6.6 rebounds and 1.9 assists and was named honorable mention [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] and the Pac-12 Most Improved Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/03/26/washington-states-robert-franks-says-hell-declare-for-nba/33306739/|title=Washington State's Robert Franks says he'll declare for NBA|work=[[USA Today|USAToday.com]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 26, 2018|access-date=July 24, 2019}}</ref> During the season he set a school record for most [[Three-point field goal|three-pointers]] made in a game with ten (on 13 attempts) against [[2017–18 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]] on January 13, 2018, scoring a then-career high 34 points in total.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2018/jan/13/analysis-robert-franks-pumps-in-school-record-10-3/|title=Analysis: Robert Franks pumps in school-record 10 3-pointers to lead Washington State past Cal|first=Theo|last=Lawson|work=The Spokesman-Review|date=January 13, 2018|access-date=July 24, 2019}}</ref> Following the season Franks declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]], but did not hire an agent.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2766716-robert-franks-declares-for-2018-nba-draft-after-3-seasons-at-washington-state|title=Robert Franks Declares for 2018 NBA Draft After 3 Seasons at Washington State|first=Rob|last=Goldberg|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=March 26, 2018|access-date=July 24, 2019}}</ref> He ultimately withdrew from the draft after deciding to return to Washington State for his senior season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/arizona-s-pac--competition-stiffens-with-wsu-s-franks/article_c02a3576-644d-11e8-bd24-7b48655b5626.html|title=Arizona's Pac-12 competition stiffens with WSU's Franks, UCLA's Hands and UW's Dickerson returning|first=Bruce|last=Pascoe|work=[[Arizona Daily Star]]|date=May 30, 2018|access-date=July 24, 2019}}</ref> As a senior Franks played in 27 games (26 starts) for Washington State, missing five games due to injury, and averaged a conference-best 21.6 points per game (24th highest in the nation) and finished with the ninth-highest rebounding average with 7.2 per game and was named first team All-Pac-12 and became the first WSU player to be named to the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] All-District 20 team since [[Brock Motum]] in 2012.<ref name="report">{{cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2019/jun/21/report-washington-states-robert-franks-agrees-to-t/|title=Report: Washington State's Robert Franks agrees to two-way deal with Charlotte Hornets|first=Theo|last=Lawson|work=The Spokesman-Review|date=June 21, 2019|access-date=July 24, 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Charlotte Hornets / Greensboro Swarm (2019–2020)===
Franks worked out for several teams and participated in the [[NBA G League]] Elite Camp before the [[2019 NBA draft]], but was not selected.<ref name="report"/> Franks signed a two-way contract with the [[Charlotte Hornets]] and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Greensboro Swarm]] on July 3, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/charlotte-hornets-sign-robert-franks-two-way-contract|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Robert Franks To Two-Way Contract|first=Quinton|last=Walsh|website=NBA.com|date=July 3, 2019|access-date=July 24, 2019}}</ref> On January 15, 2020, the [[Charlotte Hornets]] announced that they had waived Franks, without his appearing in a game for the parent team.<ref>{{cite web|first=Quinton|last=Walsh|title=Hornets Waive Robert Franks|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/hornets-waive-robert-franks|date=January 15, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 15, 2020}}</ref> He averaged 18.5 points, 5.6 rebounds and 1.6 assists per game for the Swarm.<ref>{{cite news |title=Robert Franks: Picked up by Swarm on G League deal |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/robert-franks-picked-up-by-swarm-on-g-league-deal/ |access-date=May 22, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 4, 2020}}</ref>

===Stockton Kings (2020)===
On February 4, 2020, Franks was traded to the [[Stockton Kings]] in exchange for the returning player rights to [[Daniel Ochefu]] and the Kings' first-round pick in the 2020 G League draft.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Trujillo |first1=Justin |title=Greensboro Completes Trade With Stockton |url=https://greensboro.gleague.nba.com/news/greensboro-completes-trade-with-stockton/ |access-date=February 4, 2020 |work=NBA.com |date=February 4, 2020}}</ref> On February 19, Franks recorded 29 points and 10 rebounds in a loss to the [[Agua Caliente Clippers]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Hornets' Robert Franks: Posts another big game Wednesday |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/hornets-robert-franks-posts-another-big-game-wednesday/ |access-date=May 22, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 20, 2020}}</ref>

===Lakeland / Orlando Magic (2021)===
On November 27, 2020, Franks signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Five|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-jordan-bone-karim-mane-devin-cannady-robert-franks-jon-teske-20201127|date=November 27, 2020|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 27, 2020}}</ref> He was waived at the conclusion of training camp, but added to the roster of their G League affiliate, the [[Lakeland Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|title= Lakeland Magic Finalize Roster|url= https://lakeland.gleague.nba.com/news/lakeland-magic-finalize-roster/|date=January 24, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 25, 2021}}</ref> He played in 14 games and averaged 12.1 points, 6.6 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 24.5 minutes, while shooting .508 from the floor and .356 from three-point range and in three playoff matches, he averaged 16 points, 8 rebounds and 1 assist in 29.7 minutes, while shooting .581 from the field and .563 from behind the arc en route to the G League title.<ref name="ORL10D">{{cite web|title=Magic Sign Robert Franks to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/magic-sign-robert-franks-10-day-contract-20210412|date=April 12, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 12, 2021}}</ref>

On April 12, 2021, Franks signed a 10-day contract with Orlando.<ref name="ORL10D" /> On April 22, he signed a second 10-day contract,<ref>{{cite web|title=Magic Sign Robert Franks to Second 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-robert-franks-second-ten-day-contract-20210422|date=April 22, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 22, 2021}}</ref> but was waived five days later.<ref>{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Free Agent Center Moritz Wagner|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-moe-wagner-free-agent-center-20210427|date=April 27, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 28, 2021|quote=In addition, forward Robert Franks has been released from his 10-day contract.}}</ref>

===Brisbane Bullets (2021–2022)===
On August 28, 2021, Franks signed with the [[Brisbane Bullets]] in Australia for the [[2021–22 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bullets Sign Former Orlando Magic Forward Robert Franks|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/bullets-sign-former-orlando-magic-forward-robert-franks|date=August 28, 2021|website=NBL.com.au|access-date=August 28, 2021}}</ref>

===Adelaide 36ers (2022–2023)===
On June 10, 2022, Franks signed a two-year deal with the [[Adelaide 36ers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Robert Franks Signs in Adelaide|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/robert-franks-signs-in-adelaide|date=June 10, 2022|website=NBL.com.au|access-date=June 10, 2022}}</ref> He parted ways with the 36ers after one season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Franks to pursue overseas opportunity|url=https://www.adelaide36ers.com/news/franks-to-pursue-overseas-opportunity|date=July 18, 2023|website=adelaide36ers.com|access-date=July 18, 2023}}</ref>

===Hapoel Gilboa Galil (2023)===
On February 14, 2023, Franks signed with [[Hapoel Gilboa Galil]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/hapoel-galil-gilboa-inks-robert-franks/|title=Hapoel Galil Gilboa inks Robert Franks|last=|first=|date=February 14, 2023|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=February 15, 2023 |last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref>
